title: Choose the visual world for the libra docs
question: The roll assigned the Clearing House Ledger. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Clearing House Ledger
options.lineage: bank cheque clearing: security paper, ruled ledgers, cleared and returned stamps
options.thesis: Every request is a cheque presented for clearing: each policy signs off, and one refusal returns it.
options.viewport: A security-paper masthead set like a cheque face (payee: your service, amount: one decision) over a calm white column; the left rail is a ledger index with entry numbers.
options.risk: Banking can read stiff or ornamental if the guilloche creeps into the reading column.

raised.raise: State is a mark, not only a hue: ALLOW and DENY read as cleared and returned stamps with distinct shapes, legible in greyscale.
Two inks only, committed: ledger green and return red; no third accent anywhere.
One continuous ledger rule runs the page, and every section is a numbered entry pinned to it.
Every section, endpoint and status code carries a running entry number set in tabular figures.

options.label: Request for Comments
options.lineage: IETF RFC documents: header block, numbered sections, MUST and SHOULD
options.thesis: libra documented the way engineers already read protocol truth: as a numbered, normative spec.
options.viewport: An RFC header block (status, category, date) above a numbered table of contents, the column in a reading serif with section numbers hung in the margin.
options.risk: Familiar: it is where many developer-doc redesigns land, and it can feel austere.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine Explainer
options.thesis: libra explained like a friend sketching the evaluate loop on a napkin.
options.viewport: A marker headline over a doodled request → policies → verdict diagram, then panels stepping through the contract.
options.case: Engineers love this form and it explains 'what and why' fast; the api reference loses rigor.
options.risk: Reference tables and status codes feel unserious in marker, and it needs SVG art to land.

options.label: Swiss Grid Poster Wall
options.thesis: One modular grid disciplines every section; geometry is the only imagery.
options.viewport: A huge flush-left 'libra' on the module with a red bar marking the current section, reference tables snapped to the grid.
options.case: Very clear structure for reference; says little about libra itself.
options.risk: Generic: could be any product's docs once the name is covered.

options.label: Film Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Sections strung on a perforated rail.
options.viewport: A perforated rail crossing an orange field.
options.case: Service engineers don't identify with film editing; the rail fights reading order.
options.risk: A costume on a reference page.
options.kept: State is a mark, not only a hue.

options.label: Penny-press Broadside
options.thesis: The docs as one shouting sheet.
options.viewport: Wood-type headline over two rammed columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: no fit with the audience, two hard columns hurt reference reading.
options.risk: Reads as a poster, not documentation.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: A building section with a moving sunbeam.
options.viewport: One long section with sun-angle annotations.
options.case: No link to policy evaluation; a metaphor the reader must decode.
options.kept: One continuous rule with pinned annotations.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.viewport: Stacked cloud blocks with blue voids.
options.case: Loses both axes: dreamlike where engineers want precision.
options.kept: Running tally numbers on every block.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.viewport: Left nav tree, centered column, right-hand on-this-page list.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other project's docs by design.
